stem: How many of the city's blocks are classified as commercial or mixed use and will not receive a protected bike lane?
stimulus:
A city planning department sorted all 1,600 of the city's blocks by their main land use. The table shows what percent of the blocks fall in each category. Planners will add a protected bike lane to exactly 25% of the blocks that are classified as either commercial or mixed use, and to no other blocks.

City Blocks by Main Land Use
Land use | Percent of blocks
Residential | 45%
Commercial | 20%
Mixed use | 15%
Industrial | 12%
Open space | 8%
explanation: First add the two categories: commercial and mixed use together make up 20% + 15% = 35% of the blocks, and $0.35 \times 1{,}600 = 560$ blocks. A bike lane goes on 25% of those 560 blocks, so 75% of them get no bike lane: $0.75 \times 560 = 420$. The question asks about the blocks that will not receive a lane, so you need the 75% part, not the 25% part.

A.why: This is 25% of 560, which counts the commercial and mixed-use blocks that will get a bike lane. The question asks for the ones that will not.

B.why: You took 25% of all 1,600 blocks. The 25% applies only to the 560 commercial and mixed-use blocks, and this answer also counts blocks that get a lane instead of blocks that don't.

D.why: 560 is the total number of commercial and mixed-use blocks. You stopped there and never removed the 25% of those blocks that will get a bike lane.

stem: How many tales in the archive are trickster tales?
stimulus: A folklore archive holds 1,200 recorded tales. Of these, 35% are classified as animal tales. Of the tales that are not animal tales, 30% are classified as trickster tales. No tale is placed in more than one category.
explanation: The 30% is a percent of the tales that are not animal tales, so find that group first. Animal tales are 35% of the archive, which leaves 65%: $0.65 \times 1{,}200 = 780$ tales. Trickster tales are 30% of these: $0.30 \times 780 = 234$.

A.why: You took 30% of the 420 animal tales ($0.35 \times 1{,}200$). The 30% belongs to the tales that are not animal tales, so you applied it to the wrong group.

C.why: You took 30% of all 1,200 tales. The text gives 30% of the tales that are not animal tales, so the base should be 780, not 1,200.

D.why: This is 70% of the 780 non-animal tales, which counts the tales that are neither animal tales nor trickster tales. The question asks for the trickster tales.

stem: How many bolts in the inventory are undyed wool?
stimulus: A textile museum lists 1,200 bolts of cloth from a nineteenth-century mill. Of these bolts, 35% are wool, and 40% of the wool bolts are dyed.
explanation: Wool bolts: $0.35(1{,}200) = 420$. The wool bolts that are not dyed make up $100\% - 40\% = 60\%$ of them, so $0.60(420) = 252$.

A.why: You found the dyed wool bolts, $0.40(420) = 168$. The question asks for the wool bolts that are not dyed.

C.why: 420 is every wool bolt. You stopped before taking out the dyed ones.

D.why: You took 60% of all 1,200 bolts. The 60% applies only to the wool bolts, not to the whole inventory.

stem: How many of the tagged parrotfish and wrasse were not recaptured?
stimulus:
Marine biologists tagged 800 fish on a reef. Of the tagged parrotfish and wrasse combined, 15% were recaptured later.
Tagged Fish by Species
Species | Percent of tagged fish
Parrotfish | 22%
Wrasse | 18%
Grouper | 35%
Snapper | 25%
explanation: Parrotfish and wrasse make up $22\% + 18\% = 40\%$ of the fish, and $0.40(800) = 320$. Of these, $85\%$ were not recaptured: $0.85(320) = 272$.

A.why: You found the recaptured fish, $0.15(320) = 48$. The question asks for the fish that were not recaptured.

C.why: 320 is every tagged parrotfish and wrasse. You still have to take out the 15% that were recaptured.

D.why: You took 85% of all 800 fish. The recapture rate applies only to the parrotfish and wrasse.

stem: How many sherds from the excavation are decorated?
stimulus: An excavation recovered pottery sherds from two soil layers. The 480 sherds from the lower layer make up 60% of all the sherds recovered. Overall, 15% of all the sherds are decorated.
explanation: First find the total number of sherds. $0.60x = 480$, so $x = 800$. The decorated sherds are $0.15(800) = 120$.

A.why: You took 15% of the 480 lower-layer sherds. The 15% is a share of all the sherds, so you need the total of 800.

C.why: You found the undecorated sherds, $0.85(800) = 680$. The question asks for the decorated ones.

D.why: 800 is the total number of sherds. You stopped before taking 15% of it.

stem: How many of the clinic's patients did not receive a flu vaccine?
stimulus: A clinic serves 3,000 patients, and 40% of them are over age 65. This season, 30% of the patients over 65 and 20% of the other patients received a flu vaccine.
explanation: There are $0.40(3{,}000) = 1{,}200$ patients over 65 and $1{,}800$ others. The number vaccinated is $0.30(1{,}200) + 0.20(1{,}800) = 360 + 360 = 720$, so $3{,}000 - 720 = 2{,}280$ patients were not vaccinated.

A.why: 720 is the number of patients who were vaccinated. The question asks for the patients who were not.

B.why: 1,440 counts only the unvaccinated patients age 65 or younger, $0.80(1{,}800)$. You left out the 840 unvaccinated patients over 65.

C.why: You averaged 30% and 20% to get 25%. The two groups are different sizes, so the overall rate is $720/3{,}000 = 24\%$, not 25%.

stem: How many of the deck panels were cracked in 2025?
stimulus: A bridge deck is made of 1,400 concrete panels. In 2024, 8% of the panels were cracked. In 2025, the percent of panels that were cracked was 25% greater than it was in 2024. No panels were added or removed.
explanation: A percent that is 25% greater than 8% is $8\% \times 1.25 = 10\%$. Then $0.10(1{,}400) = 140$ panels.

A.why: 28 is the increase, $0.25(112)$. The question asks for the total number of cracked panels in 2025.

B.why: 112 is the 2024 count, $0.08(1{,}400)$. You haven't applied the increase.

D.why: You added 25 percentage points to get 33%. "25% greater than 8%" means $1.25 \times 8\% = 10\%$.

stem: How many minutes of the session are spent at high intensity?
stimulus: A sprinter's training session lasts 90 minutes. The first 20% of the session is a warm-up, and the rest is the main set. During the main set, 35% of the time is spent at high intensity.
explanation: The main set takes up $80\%$ of the session: $0.80(90) = 72$ minutes. High intensity is $0.35(72) = 25.2$ minutes.

B.why: You took 35% of the full 90 minutes. The 35% applies only to the main set, so the warm-up has to come out first.

C.why: 46.8 is the part of the main set that is not high intensity, $0.65(72)$.

D.why: 72 is the length of the main set. You stopped before taking 35% of it.

stem: How many prints in the edition are offered for sale?
stimulus: A printmaker pulls an edition of 250 woodcut prints. Of these, 8% are rejected as flawed. The printmaker keeps 10% of the prints that pass as artist's proofs, and every other print that passes is offered for sale.
explanation: Accepted prints: $0.92(250) = 230$. The printmaker keeps 10% of those, so $0.90(230) = 207$ are offered for sale.

A.why: 23 is the number of artist's proofs kept, $0.10(230)$, not the number offered for sale.

B.why: You added 8% and 10% and took 82% of 250. The 10% is a share of the 230 accepted prints, not of all 250.

D.why: 230 is the number of accepted prints. You still have to take out the artist's proofs.

stem: How many sheets in the series are at the 1:50,000 scale, unrevised, or both?
stimulus:
A national atlas office keeps a series of 480 map sheets. The table shows what percent of the 480 sheets falls into each category.
Map Sheets by Scale and Status
Scale | Revised | Unrevised
1:25,000 | 15% | 25%
1:50,000 | 20% | 10%
1:100,000 | 10% | 20%
explanation: 1:50,000 sheets make up $20\% + 10\% = 30\%$ of the series, and unrevised sheets make up $25\% + 10\% + 20\% = 55\%$. The unrevised 1:50,000 sheets (10%) are in both groups, so count them once: $30\% + 55\% - 10\% = 75\%$. Then $0.75(480) = 360$.

A.why: 120 is 25% of 480: the sheets that are neither 1:50,000 nor unrevised.

B.why: 264 counts only the unrevised sheets, $0.55(480)$. You left out the revised 1:50,000 sheets.

D.why: You added 30% and 55% to get 85%. That counts the unrevised 1:50,000 sheets twice.
